messages.content: Southwest just canceled my Thursday nonstop home from Kansas City. I am still here for the installation, and I cannot leave before the lender inspection ends at 3:00. Please look at what they are offering and tell me whether I should still get home Thursday or stay another night.

I found three workable paths after the inspection. Thursday has a 5:35 p.m. departure connecting in St. Louis and arriving Atlanta at 9:58 p.m., or a 7:20 p.m. nonstop to Nashville arriving at 8:52 p.m. followed by a long drive. The next Kansas City-Atlanta nonstop leaves Friday at 7:10 a.m. and arrives at 10:05 a.m. I am checking connection details, rebooking terms, ground transportation, and the Cascade's extension rate before comparing them.

Start with the nonstop. For museum work trips I generally want the simplest routing, especially when the schedule is already disrupted. But compare all three because I may not get approval for another hotel night.

The Friday nonstop is the cleanest operationally: Kansas City at 7:10 a.m., Atlanta at 10:05 a.m., with no connection. It requires extending the Cascade through Friday checkout and leaving the hotel around 5:20 a.m. The hotel has one room in your current category Thursday night for $249 plus $49.74 in tax and fees, or $298.74 total. That rate is higher than each night on the existing reservation.
What is the real risk on the St. Louis option? Forty minutes on paper can disappear quickly.

It departs Kansas City at 5:35 p.m. Central, reaches St. Louis at 6:30, and continues at 7:12, leaving 42 minutes. Both flights use Terminal 2, but the arriving and departing gates are not assigned. If the first flight is on time, the connection is legal and should not require a terminal change. A delay of roughly 20 minutes would make it tight, and this is the last Southwest itinerary from St. Louis to Atlanta that night. Missing it would likely mean an overnight in St. Louis and arrival Friday instead.
So that gives me the worst kind of uncertainty after a full install day. What about Nashville? Include the drive and the time I would actually reach home.

The Nashville flight leaves Kansas City at 7:20 p.m. Central and arrives at 8:52 p.m. Central. A prearranged car from Nashville airport to your Atlanta address is currently quoted at $410 including estimated tolls and gratuity. The drive is about 250 miles and typically takes three hours 45 minutes at that hour, putting you home near 1:45 a.m. Eastern if baggage and pickup are prompt. A one-way rental is cheaper at about $176 plus fuel, but it adds the burden of driving after the installation and returning the car.
Do not use the rental-car version. Is Southwest actually willing to put the Nashville flight on this ticket, and would they pay for the car?

Southwest confirmed that the cancellation waiver permits a no-fare-difference change to either the Thursday St. Louis itinerary or the Friday Kansas City-Atlanta nonstop. Nashville is outside the original city pair, but an agent will authorize it as an alternate airport for this disruption without an airfare increase. The ground transfer is not included. The agent said a reimbursement request could be submitted because the cancellation is coded operational, but approval and the amount are not guaranteed. I would treat the $410 as an added trip cost unless Southwest approves it in writing.
And if I decline all of these and buy another airline? I need the exact refund position, not just a credit.

Because Southwest canceled the flight, you may decline rebooking and request a refund of the unused return segment to the museum travel card ending in 1842. The carrier currently values that unused segment at $226. It would not pay the fare difference on a replacement ticket from another airline. I checked the remaining Thursday nonstop inventory elsewhere; the only departure after 3:00 is at 4:18 p.m., which does not leave enough reliable time to finish the inspection, collect your bag, and reach the airport.
All right. Please compare the three viable choices in one place, including costs the museum would have to absorb.

Friday nonstop: arrive Atlanta 10:05 a.m. Friday; no connection risk; one extra hotel night at $298.74, plus transport to the airport; lowest travel complexity. Thursday via St. Louis: arrive Atlanta 9:58 p.m. Thursday if on time; no added airfare or hotel; 42-minute connection with no later Atlanta flight if missed. Thursday via Nashville: reach home about 1:45 a.m. Friday; no flight connection, but a 250-mile ground transfer; approximately $410 added for the car, with reimbursement uncertain. The Friday nonstop has the most predictable arrival, while St. Louis is the least expensive if it operates smoothly.
Does the Cascade require me to change the whole reservation to add Thursday, or can they extend it separately? I do not want the original three nights repriced.

They can append Thursday night to confirmation CPK-714582 without repricing Monday through Wednesday. The original guaranteed total remains $855.71, and the additional night would be charged separately at $298.74. You would keep the same room. The extension can be canceled without charge until 6:00 p.m. Central today; after that, the added night becomes nonrefundable. The hotel can place a courtesy hold on the extension until 4:00 p.m. today without charging the card.
Place that courtesy hold. I still need our registrar to approve the extra night. Do not alter the flight yet.

The Cascade has placed the Thursday-night extension on courtesy hold under the existing confirmation through 4:00 p.m. Central today. The held total is $298.74, the same room is retained, and the museum card has not been charged. Your Southwest ticket remains unchanged in disrupted status; no replacement flight has been selected.
Can Southwest preserve both the Thursday connection and Friday nonstop while I wait? I should have an answer within two hours.

They cannot hold two replacement itineraries simultaneously. The agent can leave the ticket unexchanged while you decide, but seats on both flights remain subject to availability. At present the Thursday connection has nine seats available and the Friday nonstop has more than nine. I recorded the exact flight options and rebooking authorization in the case, but that does not reserve inventory.
Then which one is more likely to disappear first? I need to know whether waiting for approval is reasonable.

The Thursday itinerary is more exposed because only nine seats remain across its two segments, and every passenger needs space on both. The Friday nonstop currently has broader availability. Waiting two hours is reasonable but not risk-free. Changing now to Thursday would protect that seat, but moving again to Friday would require availability at the time of the second change. Since Friday also depends on work approval, leaving the ticket open avoids committing you prematurely.

Leave it open. Keep the Thursday St. Louis itinerary and the Friday nonstop as the two candidates. Drop Nashville; the ground transfer is too expensive and gets me home too late. Note that I am requesting approval for the $298.74 extension and will decide before the hotel hold expires.

The plan is narrowed to two unbooked replacement options: Thursday via St. Louis, departing Kansas City at 5:35 p.m. and arriving Atlanta at 9:58 p.m. with a 42-minute connection; or Friday nonstop, departing at 7:10 a.m. and arriving at 10:05 a.m. The Nashville route is removed from consideration. The Cascade's $298.74 Thursday-night extension remains on courtesy hold until 4:00 p.m. Central, and the Southwest ticket remains open under the cancellation waiver. No flight has been changed, and both air options must be rechecked when your approval arrives.
